Content:
The intersection of two sets [MATH: A] and [MATH: B,] denoted by [MATH: A \cap B,] is the set of all elements belonging to both [MATH: A] and [MATH: B.]

Content:
For example, consider the sets [MATH: A = \{ a,b,c \}] and [MATH: B = \{ b, d, e \}.] We can represent these sets using a Venn diagram, as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d9494d14edda639e396ee3d24f58cd30]

Content:
The intersection [MATH: A \cap B] consists of all the elements that are in both [MATH: A] and [MATH: B.] To represent [MATH: A \cap B,] we will shade in all the area that is contained within both [MATH: A] and [MATH: B.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/38be2d19e1a652721ffb08339a929136]

Content:
The only element that is contained in both [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] is [MATH: b.] Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: A \cap B = \{ b \}.]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Intersections Without Venn Diagrams

Content:
